Method of Attack: Backdoor Windows systems by hijacking the Windows Boot Manager since 2012
Persistence on EFI System Partition by loading unsigned driver to bypass Windows Driver Signature Enforcement
Loading two payloads (WinSys.dll and Client.dll) that can download and execute additional malware
WinSys.dll acts as update agent communicating with command-and-control server for commands and payloads
Client.dll acts as backdoor with automatic data exfiltration including keylogging, document stealing, and screen monitoring
Altering MBR code for persistence on Legacy Boot modes
Disabling Secure Boot to patch Windows Boot Manager (bootmgfw.efi)
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with UEFI and legacy BIOS boot modes
Attack Vector: Loading unsigned driver on EFI System Partition
Disabling Secure Boot via physical access, pre-disabled Secure Boot, or exploiting UEFI firmware vulnerabilities
Indicators of Compromise: Unsigned driver on EFI System Partition
Altered MBR code in legacy BIOS systems
